m4.offPointGenuinelyIrrelevant: 30 CFR 56.15005 addresses fall protection and lifeline attendance on entry to bins, tanks or other dangerous areas. The proposition HS8 and Q9 test on M4 is whether the mill is isolated from every source of motion and blocked against rotation before entry. The section is silent on both, and a second person tending a line does not stop the shell turning. It remains tempting because it names entry into a dangerous area, which is the whole point of the trap.
m4.trapShape: ON-POINT GOVERNED AUTHORITY versus OFF-POINT GOVERNED AUTHORITY WITHIN THE APPLICABLE REGULATORY REGIME. It is NOT applicable part versus inapplicable jurisdiction, which is what it would have been had the part 57 record stayed.

records.title: Safety belts and lines
records.officialSource: eCFR current CFR text (Government Publishing Office / National Archives)
records.frozenQuotation: Safety belts and lines shall be worn when persons work where there is danger of falling; a second person shall tend the lifeline when bins, tanks, or other dangerous areas are entered.
records.officialQuotation: Safety belts and lines shall be worn when persons work where there is danger of falling; a second person shall tend the lifeline when bins, tanks, or other dangerous areas are entered.
records.finding: M4 OFF-POINT, SUBSTITUTED AT §242A. Now inside the governing part 56 regime. The official text is character-identical to the quotation frozen at §240 for the part 57 counterpart, so the provider-visible quotation is preserved exactly. Genuinely irrelevant to the proposition HS8 and Q9 test on M4: the section addresses fall protection and lifeline attendance on entry to bins, tanks or other dangerous areas, and says nothing about isolation from every source of motion or blocking against rotation, which is the whole of the M4 entry decision. Attendance by a second person does not stop the shell turning. The trap is therefore on-point authority versus off-point authority WITHIN the applicable regime, not applicable part versus inapplicable jurisdiction.
